elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience..." — covers both the master Agreement and the SOW (the Order Form analogue in this MSA structure), and is Company-only.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor" — exactly 30 days, in writing, and not conditioned on any trigger such as absence of an outstanding Statement of Work.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall refund any prepaid fees on a pro rata basis for the period after the effective date of such termination" — pro rata is expressly stated, not merely inferred from post-termination coverage.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained 6(a) grants the mutual no-cause right only "[a]t any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding"; Contractor therefore has no convenience exit while an engagement (the committed term under this MSA) is live. The insertion does not extend any Contractor right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The added right runs on thirty (30) days' notice, which is shorter than the 60–90 day fallback window (and better for us); the fallback notice term is simply not implemented.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: neither the retained Section 6 nor the insertion imposes any early-termination fee or penalty on Company for convenience termination, so there is no fee needing a cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Retained 6(a) lets Contractor terminate for any or no reason whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding; the termination effective date is not tied to the end of a then-current term. (Immaterial because the preferred level is complete.)

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Contractor's no-cause right under retained 6(a) requires only fifteen (15) days' advance notice, well short of 90 days. (Immaterial because the preferred level is complete.)

reasons: All four preferred elements are satisfied: the single inserted sentence supplies a Company-only convenience right over the Agreement or any Statement of Work, 30 days' written notice, and an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, while retained 6(a) already confines Contractor's no-cause right to periods with no outstanding Statement of Work.

The fallback level is incomplete (30-day notice rather than 60–90 days; Contractor's no-cause right is not term-end-only and carries only 15 days' notice), but that is irrelevant because the preferred checklist is fully met and position-completeness requires only one level.

Minimal: one concise insertion, no deletion of existing language, no 'in whole or in part' surplus (no Order Form/partial-termination structure requires it), no survival tail, expense language, procedure, or other model-language extras, and no duplication of the retained 6(a) or 6(b) mechanics.

Preserves intent: the mutual 15-day no-SOW right in 6(a), the material-breach right and fee/Works-in-progress consequences in 6(b), and all defined terms (Agreement, Statement of Work, Contractor, Company) survive without contradiction; 'In addition' makes clear the new right is cumulative rather than displacing 6(a).

Finding classification of 'deviation' is supportable: before the edit Company had no convenience exit while any Statement of Work was live and no prepaid-fee refund, failing both levels on the Customer side.
